chunks: And in the narration of Ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
For the bāḍiʿah, there are three camels.

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ ٱلْإِبِلِ: The prescribed compensation of three camels.
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: A transmitted hadith report or narration.
key_terms.ٱلْبَاضِعَةِ: A wound that cuts into the flesh.

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for al-bāḍiʿah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning blood money for a specific type of wound. It states that the compensation for al-bāḍiʿah is three camels, reflecting the detailed fiqh classification of bodily injuries in Islamic law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5382 - In the narration of Ibn Al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), that he said:
"For the baḍiah (a wound that cuts through the flesh after the skin), the compensation is three camels."
